title: Matching through local probes
coverage: Curated primary-source landscape of eight local-matching results under adjacency-list access, reviewed 2026-10-20. Targeted 2025–2026 searches found no later replacement for the included near-optimal LRY upper and BRR lower. Global size, stochastic oracles, and unverified historical cross-references remain separately scoped related records; this is not exhaustive coverage of every graph class or oracle model. Fixed-tree non-adaptive records are retained as skipped source metadata and omitted from the figure.
defaultScope: General unweighted simple graphs, maximum degree Delta, indexed adjacency-list probes. The main panel compares adaptive local matching queries by named guarantee and probe-formula categories. The fixed-degree panel compares n-dependence with Delta and epsilon fixed. The near-optimal comparison uses vertex-partner queries and additive deficit epsilon*n.

definitions.explicitOutput: An oracle consistent with one matching, not enumeration of all its edges. Distinguish edge-membership, matched-status, and vertex-partner queries.
definitions.sizeOutput: One estimate of the global optimum. Its total probe budget is not the same quantity as the probe budget per local matching query.
definitions.multiplicativeQuality: |M| >= (1-epsilon) OPT, or |M| >= OPT/(1+epsilon), according to the theorem.
definitions.additiveQuality: |M| >= OPT-epsilon*n; size estimates use a corresponding additive error. This gives no fixed positive multiplicative ratio when OPT is small.
definitions.probeAdaptivity: Whether the next graph probe may depend on previous answers. This is unrelated to a dynamic algorithm's adaptive adversary.
definitions.queryOrderObliviousness: Whether the matching selected by the oracle is independent of the order of user queries. This is different from non-adaptive graph probing.
definitions.nonAdaptiveTreeModel: ABGS fixes parent-index/neighbor-port instructions before exploration. The discovered vertex IDs are then followed along that fixed tree. It is stronger than fixing all vertex-ID/port pairs in advance.
definitions.edgeToPartnerConversion: Given edge-membership access of cost Q, inspecting all at most Delta incident edges gives a vertex partner in O(Delta*(Q+1)) probes. Do not silently quote Q for both outputs.
definitions.lcaToSizeConversion: Sampling O(epsilon^-2 log(1/delta)) uniformly chosen vertices and querying matched status estimates |M| to additive O(epsilon*n). With edge-membership access, account for the additional Delta factor. Sampling produces additive error, not a multiplicative estimate without a lower bound on OPT/n.
definitions.additiveNearOptimalContract: |M| >= OPT-epsilon*n. LRY gives the stronger |M| >= (1-epsilon) OPT; since OPT<=n/2, it meets this common contract. Additive deficit does not imply a fixed multiplicative ratio for sparse optima.
definitions.localVsDistributed: LCA means local computation oracle, with graph probes as the resource. Distributed LOCAL rounds are a different model; BCGS appears here only through an explicitly stated simulation.

nearOptimal.algorithmReduction: LRY edge membership is converted to partner lookup at a factor O(Delta); its multiplicative guarantee implies the displayed additive guarantee.
nearOptimal.lowerBoundWindow: 0 < epsilon <= 0.01 and log^4 n <= Delta <= n^epsilon
nearOptimal.plotType: symbolic growth orders only; no numerical hidden constants

visualCautions: An x-axis beta=1-epsilon for a theorem whose guarantee is only OPT-epsilon*n
One scalar y-axis mixing polylog(n), poly(Delta), and Delta^{O(log Delta)} without fixing parameter regimes
Plotting unspecified poly(Delta), Theta(1) quality, or O/Omega hidden constants at invented numerical coordinates
Treating edge membership, matched-status, partner, and global size as the same query
Using a non-adaptive or multigraph lower bound to shade adaptive simple-graph algorithms
Treating an average-over-random-vertices oracle analysis as a worst-case query guarantee
Showing a multiplicative inherited size guarantee for free: global sampling introduces additive error and a total-probe budget
